title: VesperStory: keeping AI-assisted development separate from game rules
author: TechnicalOutside5828
selftext:
VesperStory is an early-alpha browser town with fictional AI residents and multiplayer mini-games. This real clip shows Memory Floor.



Our development workflow gives Codex and Claude the same project bible, then separates each task into its own branch and review. The rules require tests and browser checks before gameplay is treated as ready; generated code alone is not release evidence.



One useful boundary: Memory Floor residents use seeded, imperfect memory of publicly revealed tiles, with no live AI calls or access to the hidden board.



How do you keep AI-assisted changes from breaking multiplayer timing? Try the alpha: [https://vesperstory.com](https://vesperstory.com)

comments.author: aura-32
comments.body: "Generated code alone is not release evidence" is a rule more people should steal. We ended up drawing a similar line at runtime in Hatched, the AI city sim I'm working on: citizens run on a free local rules brain by default, and the model only gets involved for moments that matter, like a job offer, a fight or a conversation. For your multiplayer mini-games, is the server the only thing allowed to decide outcomes, with the residents just reacting to what it reveals?

replies.author: TechnicalOutside5828
replies.body:
For Memory Floor, yes, the server decides the timing and outcomes



The residents work from the same public tile reveals as players, with imperfect memory so they can make mistakes too

They don’t get access to the hidden board
